To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a statistically significant increase in the incidence of cancer of the lymphatic system and of breast cancer among female employees in the laboratory of the Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology at Karolinska hospital in Stockholm, Sweden.

the risk of hematolym-phatic cancer was increased among laboratory workers, especially among those exposed to chemicals, and that the risk of breast cancer was increased among women who had worked for many years in high-exposure laboratories.

the mortality and cancer incidence among the laboratory technicians in medical laboratories were lower than expected, but that the risk of cancer of the hematolymphatic system and breast was increased after more that 10 years of employment in laboratories with a higher probability for chemical exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exposure of laboratory personnel to chemicals and the development of methods for reducing exposure.
the effects of the environment on human health.
the effects of exposure to chemical substances in laboratories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the overall mortality and cancer risk in the cohort were not increased, but that the risk of hematol-ymphatic cancer was increased among workers exposed to chemicals in the laboratory, and that the risk of breast cancer and malignant melanoma may be increased after more than a decade of work in a high-exposure laboratory.
the results are not conclusive, and that further studies are needed. © 1999 Wiley-Liss, Inc.

the risk for cancer among laboratory employees is not increased, except for the risk for hematolymphatic tumors and melanoma.
the risks for cancer and mortality among laboratory technicians is lower than among the general population.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of cancer is not increased among workers in routine laboratory work.
laboratory technicians who are working with hazardous materials are at risk for cancer.
